info.bio:
Michigan free-rock band, founded in 1992 and active until 1999, with a brief reunion in 2002 to promote a special 10-year commemorative box set edition of their CD on Enterruption, "Freedom's just another word for never getting paid."

Messy, abrasive, loose and at their best transcendent, Gravitar forged an improv-driven path between heavy rock touchstones like the Melvins, Sabbath and Unsane with out-jazz, space rock and psychedelic noise.

scenes.name: Space-rock y psicodelia extrema de los noventa
scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: Fundiendo los estilos psicodélicos que preferían la jam libre (acid-rock, space-rock, raga-rock), muchos grupos esculpen empresas sonoras épicas: Fuzzhead, Crawlspace, Pressurehed, Farflung, Fuxa, Gravitar (el Metal Machine Music de Lou Reed con ritmo), Pelt, Primordial Undermind, Escapade y, por encima de todos, Bardo Pond (Bufo Alvarius, Amanita) y Hash Jar Tempo. Texas recupera la supremacía de la locura psicodélica (Ed Hall, Cherubs, ST 37, Mike Gunn, Charalambides, Linus Pauling Quartet, la Vas Deferens Organization de Dallas); San Francisco, la psicodelia ruidosa de Mason Jones (Trance, Subarachnoid Space). En Nueva Zelanda, Roy Montgomery (Dadamah, Dissolve), Dean Roberts, Flies Inside The Sun; en Japón, Kousokuya, Mainliner, Musica Transonic, Acid Mothers Temple, Ghost.

mentions.text: …on their debut album, Medusa Cyclone (1996). Asha Vida's Nature's Clumsy Hand (1998) stretched as far as to free-jazz and musique concrete. Gravitar (12) were the noisiest of the bunch, and one of the noisiest groups of all times. Chinga Su Corazon (1993) and Gravitar (1995), totally improvised, were maelstroms of cacophony. Truculent rock'n'roll progressions built thick walls of noise. Each piece (especially on the second album) was a symphony of spectral dissonances harking back to Throbbing Gristle's macabre "industrial" rituals.
